meaning: The comment records measured pulsatile-minus-non-pulsatile mean ICP offsets per window (+0.016 baseline, -2.106 plateau, +0.250 post) and argues that only the baseline term should ever be used as a correction, because the plateau term is dominated by the model's known-wrong 22 mmHg plateau pulse. It is a documented refusal to apply a plateau mean-ICP correction in stage A of the fit.

could_move.what: The three numbers are ROUTE C outputs of verify_fit.jl on this deck's own trajectories; if the fitted parameters in fits/m3/Model_5/fit.jl change, the offsets and the argument's magnitudes go stale.

The claim leans on a plateau pulse of 22 mmHg vs a patient pulse of 4.0 quoted from the README; if that README statement or the patient target changes, the reasoning for rejecting the -2.106 correction weakens.
Any deck comparing m5 against patient data could show a different plateau pulse mismatch and so a different sign/size of the mean offset.
Cross-model decks would carry this no-correction convention into m1/m4/m6 comparisons, where the plateau pulse error may differ.

expectation: Applying the rejected plateau correction would shift plateau mean ICP by about -2.1 mmHg in stage A; the baseline term (+0.016) is small enough to be near-negligible, and the post term (+0.250) is intermediate. Whether any of these shifts change the fitted parameters is unknown from this context.

check.why: Re-runs the ROUTE C window-by-window pulsatile minus non-pulsatile mean ICP measurement that produced the three quoted numbers, without a full re-fit, so the comment's numbers can be confirmed or found stale.
